package_info.package_versions: Prior to Dec 18, 2021 (exact versions not specified, but all before the fix)
package_info.why_malicious: The app's misconfigured exported activity allowed any other app on the device to trigger an HTTP request containing the user's Amazon access token to an attacker-controlled server, enabling full compromise of the user's Amazon account and files.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when activity is launched via intent)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<activity android:label="@ref/0x7f1300ee" android:name="com.amazon.gallery.thor.app.activity.ThorViewActivity" ... >
  <intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT"/>
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE"/>
    <data android:scheme="http"/>
    <data android:scheme="https"/>
    <data android:scheme="content"/>
    <data android:scheme="file"/>
    <data android:mimeType="video/*"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/sdp"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/vnd.apple.mpegurl"/>
    <data android:mimeType="application/x-mpegurl"/>
  </intent-filter>
</activity>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the activity is exported and can be triggered by any app via an intent, causing the app to process attacker-supplied URLs and file types.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exported activities with broad intent-filters allow untrusted apps to interact with sensitive app components.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal activities should not be exported unless necessary, and should not process untrusted input without validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps export activities for deep linking or sharing, but should restrict access and sanitize input.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when activity is triggered by intent)
execution_context.file_location: com.amazon.gallery.thor.app.activity.ThorViewActivity (Java/Kotlin code, not shown, but described in report)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the activity is triggered, the app sends an HTTP request to the attacker-controlled server, including the user's Amazon access token in the x-amz-access-token header.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive tokens should never be sent to arbitrary or attacker-controlled endpoints.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Tokens should only be sent to trusted Amazon endpoints, not user-supplied URLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be sending tokens to Amazon APIs for authentication.

execution_context.file_location: External (attacker's system, using curl or similar tools)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exfiltration, the attacker uses the stolen token to access the user's Amazon profile and other APIs, retrieving or modifying sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of stolen tokens to access APIs is a classic sign of account takeover.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only the legitimate app/user should use the token; external use is unauthorized.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate API calls by the app itself.
key_indicators: Token reuse outside expected app context

attack_chain.action: Malicious app sends crafted intent to exported ThorViewActivity with attacker-controlled URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: App processes the intent and sends HTTP request.

attack_chain.action: Amazon Photos app sends HTTP request to attacker-controlled server, including user's Amazon access token in header.
Attacker uses stolen token to access Amazon APIs, retrieve personal data, and manipulate files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of user's Amazon account and files.

behavioral_signatures: Exported Android activities with broad intent-filters accepting http/https/file/content schemes
Sensitive tokens sent in HTTP headers to non-Amazon domains
Unusual API access patterns using valid tokens from unexpected IPs or user agents
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml: exported activities with VIEW/DEFAULT/BROWSABLE and http/https schemes
App code sending authentication tokens to arbitrary URLs
network_indicators: HTTP requests from Amazon Photos app to non-Amazon domains
x-amz-access-token header in requests to unknown servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor AndroidManifest.xml for exported activities with broad intent-filters. Analyze network traffic from the app for requests to non-Amazon domains containing sensitive headers (e.g., x-amz-access-token). Monitor for use of Amazon access tokens from unusual IPs or user agents, and alert on tokens used outside the expected app context.
